records.source: מִ֭שְׁלֵי שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בֶן־דָּוִ֑ד מֶ֝֗לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.
pieces: These are the proverbs of Solomon, David's son, king of Israel.

L.1: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.

R.1: These are wise sayings of Solomon, the son of David. Solomon was king of Israel.

decisions.choice: proverbs: short, memorable sayings that teach by comparison
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) covers short sayings (10:1), longer teaching poems (chapters 1–9), comparisons and even taunts (Isaiah 14:4). Its root is linked with being "like", and many proverbs teach by setting two things side by side.

decisions.choice: the proverbs of Solomon: a title for the book as a whole
decisions.reason: The title names Solomon, whose wisdom and three thousand proverbs are recorded in 1 Kings 4:29–34. The book itself also gathers "words of the wise" (22:17; 24:23), proverbs of Solomon copied by the men of Hezekiah (25:1), and the words of Agur (30:1) and of King Lemuel (31:1).

decisions.choice: wise sayings
decisions.reason: "Proverbs" may be an unfamiliar word for young readers; Readable says what they are.

records.heading: The purpose of the proverbs

records.source: לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֣ה וּמוּסָ֑ר לְ֝הָבִ֗ין אִמְרֵ֥י בִינָֽה׃
records.gloss: For knowing wisdom and discipline, for understanding sayings of understanding,
pieces: They are for learning wisdom and discipline, \q for grasping words of insight,

L.2: For knowing wisdom and discipline, \q for understanding sayings of understanding,

R.2: They will help you become wise and learn from correction. \q They will help you understand words that make things clear.

decisions.choice: wisdom: skill in living well
decisions.reason: The word (hokmah) is used for a craftsman's skill (Exodus 31:3, 6) as well as for good judgment. In Proverbs it is the skill of living rightly before God and with other people, not book learning.

decisions.choice: discipline: instruction that corrects
decisions.reason: The word (musar) means training that corrects, whether by words (1:8) or by the rod (22:15). It runs through Proverbs alongside wisdom (1:3, 7, 8).

decisions.choice: for knowing ... for understanding: the purpose of the book
decisions.reason: Verses 2–6 are a chain of phrases saying what the proverbs named in verse 1 are for. The Hebrew plays on one root: "to understand words of understanding".

decisions.choice: They are for (B); They will help you (R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew strings the purpose phrases onto the title. Balanced and Readable supply a subject so that the sentence stands on its own.

records.source: לָ֭קַחַת מוּסַ֣ר הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל צֶ֥דֶק וּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט וּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
records.gloss: For receiving discipline of insight, righteousness and justice and uprightness,
pieces: for taking in the training that brings good sense: \q righteousness, justice and fairness,

L.3: for receiving the discipline of insight, \q righteousness and justice and uprightness,

R.3: They will teach you to live with good sense, \q and to do what is right, fair and honest.

decisions.choice: discipline of insight: training that makes a person act with good sense
decisions.reason: The word (haskel) is a verb form, "acting wisely" or "having insight". Here it names what the training produces: a person who sees what to do and does it.

decisions.choice: righteousness, justice and uprightness: right dealing with others
decisions.reason: The three words often go together (2:9). Righteousness (tsedeq) is doing what is right by God and neighbor; justice (mishpat) is fair judgment; uprightness is straight, honest dealing.

decisions.choice: what is right, fair and honest
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three nouns into plain adjectives with the same meaning.

records.source: לָתֵ֣ת לִפְתָאיִ֣ם עָרְמָ֑ה לְ֝נַ֗עַר דַּ֣עַת וּמְזִמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: For giving to simple ones prudence, to a youth knowledge and discretion.
pieces: for making the naive shrewd, \q and giving the young knowledge and the ability to plan wisely.

L.4: for giving prudence to [the] simple, \q to [the] young knowledge and discretion.

R.4: They give good sense to people who are easily fooled. \q They give young people knowledge and help them plan well.

decisions.choice: simple: naive, easily led
decisions.reason: The simple (petayim) are people not yet formed, who believe whatever they hear (14:15). They are not yet set in folly, so wisdom speaks to them (1:22; 9:4). The root may mean "open", easy to persuade (compare 1:10).

decisions.choice: prudence ... discretion: shrewdness and the power to plan
decisions.reason: Both words can be used of bad cunning (the serpent is "crafty" in Genesis 3:1, the same root as prudence; schemes in 12:2). Here they are good: the shrewdness that sees through a trap, and the ability to think ahead.

decisions.choice: naive
decisions.reason: "Simple" in modern English suggests low intelligence. The Hebrew word means inexperienced and gullible, which "naive" says. Literal keeps "simple".

records.source: יִשְׁמַ֣ע חָ֭כָם וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶ֑קַח וְ֝נָב֗וֹן תַּחְבֻּל֥וֹת יִקְנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Let hear [the] wise and let him increase learning, and [the] discerning, guidance let him acquire,
pieces: Let the wise listen and gain still more learning; \q let those with understanding acquire skill to steer their way,

L.5: Let [the] wise hear and increase learning, \q and let [the] discerning acquire guidance,

R.5: Wise people should listen to them and learn even more. \q People with understanding should get good advice from them.

decisions.choice: let the wise hear: an invitation inside the list
decisions.reason: The verbs may be read as wishes ("let him hear") or as plain futures ("the wise will hear"). Either way the verse breaks into the list of purposes to say that the proverbs are not only for beginners.

decisions.choice: guidance: skill in steering
decisions.reason: The word (tahbulot) is related to the word for a ship's rope and its sailor (Ezekiel 27:8), so it pictures steering. It is the skill of finding a course through life (11:14; 24:6).

decisions.choice: skill to steer their way
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of steering that the Hebrew word carries (m2).

records.source: לְהָבִ֣ין מָ֭שָׁל וּמְלִיצָ֑ה דִּבְרֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים וְחִידֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: To understand a proverb and a figure, words of wise ones and their riddles.
pieces: so that they understand proverbs and figures of speech, \q the sayings of the wise and their riddles.

L.6: to understand a proverb and a figure, \q the words of the wise and their riddles.

R.6: Then they will understand proverbs and word pictures, \q and the sayings and riddles of wise people.

decisions.choice: figure ... riddles: sayings whose meaning must be worked out
decisions.reason: A figure (melitsah) is a saying that needs interpreting (Habakkuk 2:6). A riddle (hidah) is a puzzling saying, like Samson's (Judges 14:12) or the hard questions the queen of Sheba brought to Solomon (1 Kings 10:1).

decisions.choice: to understand: continuing verse 5
decisions.reason: The phrase may carry on the list in verses 2–4 or say what the guidance of verse 5 leads to. The sense is the same: the proverbs train readers to understand wise sayings.

records.source: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה רֵאשִׁ֣ית דָּ֑עַת חָכְמָ֥ה וּ֝מוּסָ֗ר אֱוִילִ֥ים בָּֽזוּ׃פ
records.gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [is the] beginning of knowledge; wisdom and discipline fools despise.
pieces: Knowledge begins with the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but fools treat wisdom and discipline with contempt.

L.7: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] the beginning of knowledge; \q wisdom and discipline fools despise.

R.7: Real knowledge starts with honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe. \q Fools look down on wisdom and correction.

decisions.choice: the fear of the LORD: reverent awe that trusts and obeys
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is the motto of the book (9:10; 15:33) and of its last chapter (31:30). It is not dread that runs from God but awe that turns from evil (3:7; 8:13) and trusts him (14:26).

decisions.choice: beginning: the starting point, and also the chief part
decisions.reason: The word (reshit) can mean the first of something (Genesis 1:1) or the best of it (Amos 6:6). Proverbs 9:10 says the same thing with a word that means only "beginning", so the starting point is the main sense: knowledge does not begin anywhere else.

decisions.choice: fools: people who reject correction
decisions.reason: The fool here (evil) is not slow-witted but morally stubborn: he despises discipline (15:5) and cannot keep quiet (10:14). The Hebrew puts "wisdom and discipline" first, before "fools despise", for emphasis.

decisions.choice: Knowledge begins with
alternatives: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the sentence in an order that sounds natural in English while keeping each word; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: honoring ... with awe
decisions.reason: In modern English "fear" alone suggests being afraid. Readable says what the fear of the LORD is (m1).

records.source: שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי מוּסַ֣ר אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝טֹּ֗שׁ תּוֹרַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Hear, my son, [the] discipline of your father, and do not forsake [the] teaching of your mother.
pieces: My son, listen when your father corrects you, \q and do not let go of what your mother teaches you.

L.8: Hear, my son, the discipline of your father, \q and do not let go [of] the teaching of your mother.

R.8: My son, listen when your father corrects you. \q Do not turn away from what your mother teaches you.

decisions.choice: my son: a father teaching his son
decisions.reason: Chapters 1–9 are spoken by a father to his son, with the mother's teaching beside his (4:3–4; 31:1). Teachers in the ancient Near East also called a pupil "my son", but the mention of both parents here points to a family. The advice is for every reader.

decisions.choice: teaching: a parent's instruction
decisions.reason: The word (torah) later names God's law, but its basic sense is instruction, here given by a mother (also 6:20; 31:26).

decisions.choice: my son, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The father is speaking to his son (m1), so "my son" stays at every level. The same is true wherever the address recurs (1:10, 15).

records.heading: Refuse the invitation of sinners

records.source: כִּ֤י׀לִוְיַ֤ת חֵ֓ן הֵ֬ם לְרֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲנָקִ֗ים לְגַרְגְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: For a wreath of grace they [are] for your head, and necklaces for your neck.
pieces: For they will be a lovely wreath on your head \q and ornaments hanging around your neck.

L.9: For a wreath of grace they [are] for your head, \q and pendants for your neck.

R.9: Their teaching will make you honored by others, like a beautiful wreath on your head \q or a necklace around your neck.

decisions.choice: wreath ... necklaces: signs of honor and favor
decisions.reason: A wreath on the head and a chain around the neck honored a person in public, as Pharaoh honored Joseph (Genesis 41:42). Proverbs 4:9 uses the same picture of wisdom.

decisions.choice: grace: beauty that wins favor
decisions.reason: The word (hen) means charm or beauty and the favor it wins from others (3:4; 3:22).

decisions.choice: will make you honored by others
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the picture means (m1) and keeps the picture as a comparison.

records.source: בְּנִ֡י אִם־יְפַתּ֥וּךָ חַ֝טָּאִ֗ים אַל־תֹּבֵֽא׃
records.gloss: My son, if sinners entice you, do not be willing.
pieces: My son, if sinners try to lure you, do not go along with them.

L.10: My son, if sinners entice you, do not be willing.

R.10: My son, sinful people may try to get you to join them. \q Do not agree to it.

decisions.choice: entice: persuade someone gullible
decisions.reason: The verb (patah) shares its root with "the simple" (1:4, 22, 32). Sinners entice the simple, the kind of person who can be talked into anything.

decisions.choice: do not be willing: do not consent
decisions.reason: The same verb (abah) comes back in 1:25 and 1:30: those who refuse wisdom are "not willing" to have her rebuke. The son is to refuse the sinners as firmly as fools refuse wisdom.

records.source: אִם־יֹאמְרוּ֮ לְכָ֪ה אִ֫תָּ֥נוּ נֶאֶרְבָ֥ה לְדָ֑ם נִצְפְּנָ֖ה לְנָקִ֣י חִנָּֽם׃
records.gloss: If they say, Come with us; let us lie in wait for blood; let us hide for [the] innocent without cause;
pieces: If they say, "Come with us; \q let us lie in wait to shed blood; \q let us set an ambush for the innocent, for no reason;

L.11: If they say, "Come with us; \q let us lie in wait for blood; \q let us lie hidden for [the] innocent without cause;

R.11: They may say, "Come with us! \q Let us hide and wait to kill someone. \q Let us attack an innocent person just for the fun of it.

decisions.choice: without cause: modifying the ambush
alternatives: innocent without cause: someone who has done nothing to deserve it
decisions.reason: The word (hinnam) may say the ambush is for no reason, or that the victim is innocent of any wrong. Either way the attack is unprovoked. It returns in 1:17, where the net is spread "in vain".

decisions.choice: lie in wait for blood: plan to kill
decisions.reason: "Blood" stands for a life taken (1:16, 18). The gang does not hide its aim.

decisions.choice: just for the fun of it
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the gang has no cause at all; it is a stretch beyond the Hebrew, which says only "for nothing".

records.source: נִ֭בְלָעֵם כִּשְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים כְּי֣וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Let us swallow them like Sheol alive, and whole like those going down [to the] pit;
pieces: let us gulp them down alive, as Sheol does, \q whole, like people going down into the pit;

L.12: let us swallow them like Sheol, alive, \q and whole, like those going down [to the] pit;

R.12: We will swallow them up alive, the way the grave swallows the dead. \q We will take them whole, like people going down into the pit of death.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is where all the dead go, good and bad alike (Genesis 37:35), not a place of punishment. It is pictured as a hungry mouth that is never full (27:20; 30:15–16; Isaiah 5:14).

decisions.choice: alive and whole: like Korah and his men
decisions.reason: The earth swallowed Korah and his men and they went down alive to Sheol (Numbers 16:30–33). The gang boasts it will do the same to its victims.

decisions.choice: pit: the grave, the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The pit (bor) is a cistern or dungeon, and also, as here, a name for the grave or the underworld (Psalm 28:1; Isaiah 14:15).

decisions.choice: Sheol
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew name, since no English word means the same (m1). Readable says "the grave".

records.source: כָּל־ה֣וֹן יָקָ֣ר נִמְצָ֑א נְמַלֵּ֖א בָתֵּ֣ינוּ שָׁלָֽל׃
records.gloss: All precious wealth we will find; we will fill our houses [with] plunder;
pieces: we will come away with riches of every kind \q and pack our houses with what we take;

L.13: all precious wealth we will find; \q we will fill our houses [with] plunder;

R.13: We will grab all kinds of expensive things \q and fill our houses with stolen goods.

decisions.choice: plunder: goods taken by force
decisions.reason: The word (shalal) is the spoil of war (Judges 5:30). The gang treats robbery as a campaign.

records.source: גּ֭וֹרָ֣לְךָ תַּפִּ֣יל בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ כִּ֥יס אֶ֝חָ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Your lot you will cast among us; one purse will be for all of us,
pieces: join your lot to ours; \q there will be one purse for all of us,"

L.14: your lot you will cast among us; \q one purse will be for all of us,"

R.14: Join our group, and we will all share everything we take."

decisions.choice: cast your lot among us: become one of us, with an equal share
decisions.reason: Lots were cast to divide land and goods (Joshua 18:10; Psalm 22:19). To cast one's lot with a group is to join it and share in what it gets.

decisions.choice: one purse: a shared bag of takings
decisions.reason: The purse (kis) is the bag for money and weights (16:11). The offer of an equal share is the bait.

records.source: בְּנִ֗י אַל־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אִתָּ֑ם מְנַ֥ע רַ֝גְלְךָ֗ מִנְּתִיבָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: My son, do not walk in [the] way with them; hold back your foot from their path.
pieces: my son, do not go down that road with them; \q keep your feet off their path.

L.15: my son, do not walk in the way with them; \q hold back your foot from their path.

R.15: My son, do not go with them. \q Stay far away from the way they live.

decisions.choice: do not walk: the answer to the "if" of verse 11
decisions.reason: Verses 11–14 report what the sinners say; verse 15 gives the father's reply, repeating the warning of verse 10.

decisions.choice: way ... path: a way of life
decisions.reason: In Proverbs a way or path is the course of a person's life and where it leads (1:19; 4:18–19).

records.source: כִּ֣י רַ֭גְלֵיהֶם לָרַ֣ע יָר֑וּצוּ וִֽ֝ימַהֲר֗וּ לִשְׁפָּךְ־דָּֽם׃
records.gloss: For their feet to evil run, and they hurry to shed blood.
pieces: For their feet race toward evil, \q and they are in a hurry to kill.

L.16: For their feet run to evil, \q and they hasten to pour out blood.

R.16: They are always quick to do evil. \q They hurry to kill people.

decisions.choice: keep the verse, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The verse is in the Hebrew text but missing from some of the oldest manuscripts of the Greek translation. Almost the same words are in Isaiah 59:7, which Paul quotes in Romans 3:15.

decisions.choice: shed blood: kill
decisions.reason: To pour out blood is to kill (Genesis 9:6).

records.source: כִּֽי־חִ֭נָּם מְזֹרָ֣ה הָרָ֑שֶׁת בְּ֝עֵינֵ֗י כָל־בַּ֥עַלכָּנָֽף׃
records.gloss: For in vain [is] spread the net in [the] eyes of every owner of wing.
pieces: It is useless to spread a net \q in full view of any bird.

L.17: For in vain the net is spread \q in the eyes of any winged [creature].

R.17: Even a bird knows to stay away from a trap it can see.

decisions.choice: a bird that sees the net avoids it; these men see nothing
alternatives: the bird sees the net, takes the bait and is caught anyway
the son, now warned, will not be caught by their trap
decisions.reason: The proverb is short and has been read several ways. Read with verse 18, it most likely means that even a bird will not fly into a net it can see, yet these men walk into the trap they set for others. "In vain" (hinnam) echoes "without cause" in verse 11.

decisions.choice: owner of a wing: a bird
decisions.reason: Hebrew calls a bird "an owner of a wing" (Ecclesiastes 10:20).

decisions.choice: Even a bird knows to stay away from a trap it can see
alternatives: A net is useless in front of a bird
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the reading chosen in m1; the Hebrew leaves it to the reader.

records.source: וְ֭הֵם לְדָמָ֣ם יֶאֱרֹ֑בוּ יִ֝צְפְּנ֗וּ לְנַפְשֹׁתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they for their [own] blood lie in wait; they hide for their [own] lives.
pieces: But it is their own blood they are waiting to shed; \q it is their own lives they ambush.

L.18: And they lie in wait for their [own] blood; \q they lie hidden for their [own] lives.

R.18: But these men are really setting a trap for themselves. \q They will lose their own lives.

decisions.choice: they lie in wait ... they lie hidden: the plot turned back on them
decisions.reason: The two verbs are the ones the gang used in verse 11. The violence they plan for others will fall on them (26:27; Psalm 7:16–17).

decisions.choice: lives: their own selves
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) is the living person, here their life itself, as in verse 19.

records.source: כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־בֹּ֣צֵֽעַ בָּ֑צַע אֶת־נֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלָ֣יו יִקָּֽח׃פ
records.gloss: Thus [are the] paths of everyone gaining unjust gain; the life of its owners it takes.
pieces: That is how it goes for all who grab at dishonest profit: \q their profit costs them their lives.

L.19: So [are the] paths of everyone who gains unjust gain; \q it takes the life of its owners.

R.19: This is what happens to everyone who is greedy for money they did not earn honestly. \q Their greed will end up killing them.

decisions.choice: gaining unjust gain: making profit by violence or fraud
decisions.reason: The verb and noun (betsa) are used for profit taken by force or by cheating (15:27; Ezekiel 22:27).

decisions.choice: the life of its owners: dishonest gain kills those who take it
alternatives: it takes the life of the owners of the goods (the victims)
decisions.reason: "Its owners" are those who have the gain, that is, the robbers themselves, as verse 18 has just said. Some read it of the victims, whose lives are taken with their goods, but the verse sums up where the robbers' own path leads.

records.source: חָ֭כְמוֹת בַּח֣וּץ תָּרֹ֑נָּה בָּ֝רְחֹב֗וֹת תִּתֵּ֥ן קוֹלָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Wisdom in the street cries aloud; in the squares she gives her voice.
pieces: Wisdom shouts out in the street; \q in the open squares she makes her voice heard.

L.20: Wisdom in the street cries aloud; \q in the squares she gives her voice.

R.20: Wisdom is like a woman who shouts in the streets. \q She calls out loudly in the town squares.

decisions.choice: Wisdom: pictured as a woman who speaks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for wisdom is feminine, and Proverbs pictures wisdom as a woman calling people to her (8:1–36; 9:1–6), set against the foolish woman of 9:13–18.

decisions.choice: Wisdom: a plural form meaning wisdom in its fullness
decisions.reason: The noun is plural (hokmot) but the verb is singular, so it names one person. The plural form probably stresses greatness, as it does in 9:1.

decisions.choice: the street ... the squares: the busiest public places
decisions.reason: The squares were the open spaces inside the city gates where people met, traded and held court.

decisions.choice: is like a woman who
decisions.reason: Readable says that wisdom is being pictured as a person (m1), so young readers do not miss it.

records.heading: Wisdom calls in the streets

records.source: בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הֹמִיּ֗וֹת תִּ֫קְרָ֥א בְּפִתְחֵ֖י שְׁעָרִ֥ים בָּעִ֗יר אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ תֹאמֵֽר׃
records.gloss: At [the] head of noisy [streets] she calls; at [the] openings of [the] gates in the city her sayings she says:
pieces: At the busiest corners, above the noise, she calls out; \q at the city gates where people go in and out, \q she makes her speech:

L.21: At [the] head of [the] noisy [streets] she calls out; \q at the openings of the gates in the city she speaks her sayings:

R.21: She calls out on the busy street corners and at the city gates. \q This is what she says:

decisions.choice: noisy [streets], as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means noisy or bustling places. The ancient Greek translation read "on the top of the walls", from a Hebrew word that looks much the same. Either way Wisdom speaks where she will be heard by the most people.

decisions.choice: the gates: where a town did its public business
decisions.reason: Trade, legal cases and public notices all happened at the city gate (Ruth 4:1–2; Deuteronomy 21:19). Wisdom is not a secret; she speaks where everyone passes (8:1–3).

records.source: עַד־מָתַ֣י׀פְּתָיִם֮ תְּֽאֵהֲב֫וּ פֶ֥תִי וְלֵצִ֗ים לָ֭צוֹן חָמְד֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים יִשְׂנְאוּ־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Until when, simple ones, will you love simpleness, and scoffers scoffing delight in for themselves, and fools hate knowledge?
pieces: "You naive people, how much longer will you love being naive? \q How long will mockers enjoy their mocking, \q and fools hate knowledge?

L.22: "Until when, simple ones, will you love simpleness, \q and scoffers take delight for themselves in scoffing, \q and fools hate knowledge?

R.22: "You foolish people who believe anything, how long will you be happy to stay that way? \q How long will people who make fun of what is good keep enjoying it? \q How long will fools hate knowledge?

decisions.choice: you ... they: Wisdom turns from speaking to her hearers to speaking about them
decisions.reason: Wisdom addresses the simple ("you will love"), then speaks of mockers and fools in the third person. She does the same in verses 23–28.

decisions.choice: scoffers: people who sneer at correction
decisions.reason: The scoffer (lets) will not listen to rebuke and hates the one who gives it (9:7–8; 13:1). He is the hardest of the three to teach (21:11).

decisions.choice: fools: the self-confident
decisions.reason: This word for fool (kesil) is a different one from verse 7. The kesil is the dull, self-satisfied person who does not want understanding (18:2).

decisions.choice: foolish people who believe anything
decisions.reason: Readable describes the simple by what they do (14:15) rather than naming them.

records.source: תָּשׁ֗וּבוּ לְֽת֫וֹכַחְתִּ֥י הִנֵּ֤ה אַבִּ֣יעָה לָכֶ֣ם רוּחִ֑י אוֹדִ֖יעָה דְבָרַ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: You will turn back at my rebuke; look, I will pour out to you my spirit; I will make known my words to you.
pieces: Turn back when I rebuke you, \q and I will pour out my heart to you \q and make my words known to you.

L.23: Turn back at my rebuke; \q look, I will pour out my spirit to you; \q I will make known my words to you.

R.23: Listen when I correct you, and change your ways! \q Then I will tell you everything that is in my heart. \q I will teach you what I have to say.

decisions.choice: turn back: an urgent appeal
decisions.reason: The verb is a plain future, "you will turn", which may be an appeal ("turn!") or the start of a condition ("if you turn"). The promise that follows suits both. Verse 24 shows the appeal was refused.

decisions.choice: my spirit: what is in Wisdom's mind and heart
decisions.reason: Spirit (ruah) here stands beside "my words", so Wisdom promises to pour out all she thinks and says, as a spring pours out water (18:4). It is not, in this verse, the Spirit poured out in Joel 2:28.

decisions.choice: my heart
decisions.reason: In English "pour out my spirit" calls to mind God's Spirit; "pour out my heart" says what Wisdom means (m2). Literal keeps "spirit".

records.source: יַ֣עַן קָ֭רָאתִי וַתְּמָאֵ֑נוּ נָטִ֥יתִי יָ֝דִ֗י וְאֵ֣ין מַקְשִֽׁיב׃
records.gloss: Because I called and you refused; I stretched out my hand and there [was] no one paying attention,
pieces: But since I called and you would not come, \q since I held out my hand and no one took notice,

L.24: Because I called and you refused, \q I stretched out my hand and there was no one paying attention,

R.24: I called to you, but you would not come. \q I reached out my hand to you, but no one paid any attention.

decisions.choice: because: the reason for what Wisdom will do in verses 26–28
decisions.reason: Verses 24–25 give the cause; verse 26 the result. Wisdom's offer was made and refused.

decisions.choice: stretched out my hand: beckoned
decisions.reason: Here the gesture invites people to come (Isaiah 65:2).

records.source: וַתִּפְרְע֥וּ כָל־עֲצָתִ֑י וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you neglected all my counsel, and my rebuke you were not willing,
pieces: since you brushed aside all my advice \q and would have no part of my correction,

L.25: and you neglected all my counsel, \q and my rebuke you were not willing [to have],

R.25: You ignored all my advice. \q You did not want me to correct you.

decisions.choice: neglected: let go, threw off
decisions.reason: The verb (para) means to let loose or leave unattended (4:15; 13:18).

decisions.choice: you were not willing: you refused
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 1:10: the son must not be willing to join sinners, but these people were not willing to accept Wisdom.

records.source: גַּם־אֲ֭נִי בְּאֵידְכֶ֣ם אֶשְׂחָ֑ק אֶ֝לְעַ֗ג בְּבֹ֣א פַחְדְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Also I at your calamity will laugh; I will mock when your dread comes,
pieces: so when ruin comes to you, I too will laugh; \q when the thing you dread arrives, I will jeer,

L.26: I also at your calamity will laugh; \q I will mock when your dread comes,

R.26: So I will laugh when trouble comes to you. \q I will make fun of you when the thing you are afraid of happens.

decisions.choice: laugh ... mock: the scorn of the scornful turned back on them
alternatives: Wisdom takes pleasure in their suffering
decisions.reason: Wisdom answers mockers in their own terms (3:34), as the LORD laughs at the nations who plot against him (Psalm 2:4). The point is that the time for listening has passed, not that their pain pleases her.

decisions.choice: your dread: the disaster you fear
decisions.reason: Dread (pahad) here is what is dreaded, the trouble itself (also 1:27; 3:25).

records.source: בְּבֹ֤א כְשׁוֹאָ֨ה׀פַּחְדְּכֶ֗ם וְֽ֭אֵידְכֶם כְּסוּפָ֣ה יֶאֱתֶ֑ה בְּבֹ֥א עֲ֝לֵיכֶ֗ם צָרָ֥ה וְצוּקָֽה׃
records.gloss: When comes like a storm your dread, and your calamity like a whirlwind arrives, when comes on you trouble and distress.
pieces: when terror sweeps over you like a storm \q and ruin like a whirlwind, \q when trouble and hardship close in on you.

L.27: when your dread comes like a storm, \q and your calamity like a whirlwind arrives, \q when trouble and distress come upon you.

R.27: Terror will hit you like a storm. \q Trouble will come at you like a whirlwind. \q You will be in pain and distress.

decisions.choice: like a storm, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text and the reading the scribes marked for it (ketiv and qere) spell this word slightly differently. Both mean a storm or sudden ruin.

decisions.choice: trouble and distress: being hemmed in
decisions.reason: Both words come from roots meaning narrow or tight: the pressure of trouble with no way out.

records.source: אָ֣ז יִ֭קְרָאֻנְנִי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה יְ֝שַׁחֲרֻ֗נְנִי וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָאֻֽנְנִי׃
records.gloss: Then they will call me, and I will not answer; they will seek me earnestly, and not find me.
pieces: Then they will cry out to me, but I will give no answer; \q they will search hard for me without finding me.

L.28: Then they will call me, and I will not answer; \q they will seek me earnestly, and they will not find me.

R.28: Then they will call to me for help, but I will not answer. \q They will look everywhere for me, but they will not find me.

decisions.choice: they: Wisdom now speaks about her hearers
decisions.reason: Wisdom turns from "you" to "they", as if speaking to others about those who refused her (see 1:22).

decisions.choice: seek earnestly: search with effort
decisions.reason: The verb (shahar) is related to the word for dawn, and older translations render it "seek early". Its sense is eager searching (8:17).

records.source: תַּ֭חַת כִּי־שָׂ֣נְאוּ דָ֑עַת וְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה לֹ֣א בָחָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Because they hated knowledge, and the fear of YHWH they did not choose,
pieces: All this because they hated knowledge, \q and the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not what they chose.

L.29: Because they hated knowledge, \q and the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they did not choose,

R.29: This will happen because they hated knowledge. \q They chose not to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe.

decisions.choice: did not choose the fear of the LORD: a decision, not ignorance
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD, the beginning of knowledge (1:7), was offered to them, and they chose against it. The section ends where it began.

decisions.choice: All this because
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the reason a sentence of its own; "all this" points back to verse 28.

records.source: לֹא־אָב֥וּ לַעֲצָתִ֑י נָ֝אֲצ֗וּ כָּל־תּוֹכַחְתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: They were not willing for my counsel; they despised all my rebuke.
pieces: They refused my advice \q and treated every correction I gave with contempt.

L.30: they were not willing [to have] my counsel; \q they despised all my rebuke,

R.30: They did not want my advice. \q They hated it when I corrected them.

decisions.choice: despised: rejected with scorn
decisions.reason: The verb (naats) is used of treating God or his word with contempt (5:12; Numbers 14:11).

records.source: וְֽ֭יֹאכְלוּ מִפְּרִ֣י דַרְכָּ֑ם וּֽמִמֹּעֲצֹ֖תֵיהֶ֣ם יִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will eat from [the] fruit of their way, and from their schemes they will be sated.
pieces: So they will eat what their own way of life has produced \q and have more than enough of their own schemes.

L.31: And they will eat from the fruit of their way, \q and from their schemes they will be sated.

R.31: So they will get what is coming to them for the way they lived. \q They will have more than enough of their own plans.

decisions.choice: eat the fruit of their way: live with the results of how they lived
decisions.reason: What people do bears fruit that they themselves must eat (12:14; 18:20; Isaiah 3:10).

decisions.choice: be sated: be filled, even to disgust
decisions.reason: The verb (saba) can mean filled to the point of sickness (25:16). They will have their fill of their own plans.

decisions.choice: get what is coming to them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of eating fruit means (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י מְשׁוּבַ֣ת פְּתָיִ֣ם תַּֽהַרְגֵ֑ם וְשַׁלְוַ֖ת כְּסִילִ֣ים תְּאַבְּדֵֽם׃
records.gloss: For [the] turning away of simple ones will kill them, and [the] ease of fools will destroy them.
pieces: The naive turn away, and it kills them; \q fools feel safe and at ease, and it destroys them.

L.32: For [the] turning away of [the] simple will kill them, \q and [the] ease of fools will destroy them.

R.32: People who believe anything turn away from wisdom, and it will kill them. \q Fools feel safe and do not worry, and that will destroy them.

decisions.choice: turning away: turning their backs on Wisdom
decisions.reason: The word (meshubah) is used of Israel turning away from the LORD (Jeremiah 3:22). Here it is the simple turning from Wisdom's call.

decisions.choice: ease: careless security
decisions.reason: The word (shalvah) is quiet and ease, and here the false sense of safety of people who think nothing can touch them (Ezekiel 16:49).

decisions.choice: The naive turn away, and it kills them
alternatives: The turning away of the naive will kill them
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the Hebrew nouns into verbs, which English handles more easily.

records.source: וְשֹׁמֵ֣עַֽ לִ֭י יִשְׁכָּן־בֶּ֑טַח וְ֝שַׁאֲנַ֗ן מִפַּ֥חַד רָעָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: But one listening to me will dwell [in] security and be at ease from dread of harm.
pieces: But anyone who listens to me will live securely, \q at rest and free from the fear of harm."

L.33: But one who listens to me will dwell [in] security \q and be at ease from dread of harm."

R.33: But people who listen to me will be safe. \q They will live in peace and will not be afraid of trouble."

decisions.choice: in security: safe and with nothing to fear
decisions.reason: The word (betah) means both safety and the confidence that comes with it (3:23; 10:9).

decisions.choice: one who listens: the end of Wisdom's speech, set against verse 32
decisions.reason: Wisdom's speech ends with a promise. Those who listen live at ease without dread, while the ease of fools destroys them (verse 32) and the dread they feared comes on them (verses 26–27).
